data.narrative:
ICON, a Series C-stage company in Housing & Construction led by founder Kennan Frost, has raised $450M+ to date. The comparable universe is limited, consisting of one identified private peer (Meter) and no public comparables in the immediate sector, which constrains triangulation depth.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the $450M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage progression, this method yields an implied valuation of $765M. This reflects observed expansion multiples in venture-backed hardware and infrastructure companies at similar funding inflection points.

The triangulated range derived from available methodology spans $650M (low) to $880M (high), with a median point estimate of $765M. The narrow methodological base—one method, one private comparable, no public reference points—represents a material limitation. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue multiples or comparable exit precedents in residential construction technology, the early-stage nature of the market segment, and execution risk inherent in Series C infrastructure ventures. The valuation is most defensible as a forward-looking capital-structure marker rather than a market-derived fair-value estimate. Additional data on burn rate, path to profitability, and sector-specific SaaS or hardware multiples would sharpen confidence in this range.
